investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state and the eval runner never advanced past the scheduling step.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod is stuck in Unschedulable state. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner calls createAgent with machineType "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885), the resulting pod cannot be placed, and the probe times out without ever writing any required evidence fields.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new pods. Preemption found no victims, indicating no lower-priority pods are present to evict.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector rules, artificially constraining scheduling to only 2 nodes. If the selector is overly restrictive, even partial VM capacity on other nodes would be unreachable.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm slots across the cluster (limited to 2 nodes) is insufficient to absorb concurrent eval probe requests plus any live workload, causing contention during the eval window.

Lower probability — a recent change to pod spec resource requests or node affinity labels (not evidenced in suspectChanges, which is empty) could have altered scheduling behavior, but no suspect commit is present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to support this hypothesis.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation on the 2 eligible nodes immediately to determine current capacity vs. demand. If slots are fully occupied, identify which pods hold them and whether any are stale, leaked, or eligible for eviction.

Check for leaked or zombie remote-agent pods that may be holding VM slots without active workloads. The eval runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883), but if a prior run was interrupted, cleanup may not have completed.

Evaluate whether the node affinity/selector rules that exclude 4 of 6 nodes from remote-agent scheduling are intentional. If those 4 nodes could be made eligible (e.g., by adding the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource or adjusting labels), effective capacity would increase.

Assess whether the cluster needs additional nodes with kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity to handle concurrent eval probes plus live workload. The current 2-node constraint creates a single point of contention.

Once cluster capacity is restored or freed, re-run the eval suite to confirm all three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) return to a passing state with all required evidence fields populated.

Note: this is an eval-layer failure reflecting a real infrastructure scheduling constraint. There is no user-traffic or incident signal in the supplied evidence, so impact should be scoped to the observability eval and the remote-agent provisioning path until further signals are available.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is available and not exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a different scheduling constraint (e.g., taint, label mismatch, quota) must be investigated.

If re-running the eval probe immediately after the failure succeeds and produces all required evidence fields, the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly occupied slot) rather than sustained exhaustion.

If the 4 nodes that 'didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' are shown to have kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the affinity rules are found to be misconfigured (not intentional), the primary cause shifts to a node selector/affinity misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.

If no existing pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm resources on the 2 eligible nodes, the resource may be misconfigured or the node resource advertisement may have stopped, which would be a different failure mode than exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-create fails while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime pass in a subsequent run, the failure is not cluster-wide and may be isolated to a specific pod spec or timing window.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm resource availability across all cluster nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, so scheduling exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct infrastructure check rather than a timeout inside the agent-create probe.
Add a cluster node capacity eval that asserts at least N kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are free across the eligible node pool, alerting before the pool is fully exhausted.

Add a remote-agent pod cleanup verification eval that confirms no orphaned remote-agent pods are holding VM slots after each eval run cycle, catching cleanup failures from interrupted withCleanup paths.

Add a node affinity coverage eval that asserts the fraction of cluster nodes matching the remote-agent pod selector meets a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 50% of nodes), catching affinity misconfigurations before they cause full scheduling failures.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-25T09:47–09:52Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the probe pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs:1905) never returned an agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written, causing the expected-output contract to be fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent provisioning path has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, so no node in the 6-node cluster can accept the pod. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the eligible nodes. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure that prevents any remote agent pod from being created, which in turn prevents the eval runner from obtaining an agentId or polling agent state. This is an eval-detected infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state and the eval runner never advanced past the scheduling step.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod is stuck in Unschedulable state. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner calls createAgent with machineType "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885), the resulting pod cannot be placed, and the probe times out without ever writing any required evidence fields.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=131227, pod stuck unscheduled for 126s before the check ended at 2026-06-25T09:47:35.925Z
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was written, consistent with the pod never starting

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never schedules
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new pods. Preemption found no victims, indicating no lower-priority pods are present to evict.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector rules, artificially constraining scheduling to only 2 nodes. If the selector is overly restrictive, even partial VM capacity on other nodes would be unreachable.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm slots across the cluster (limited to 2 nodes) is insufficient to absorb concurrent eval probe requests plus any live workload, causing contention during the eval window.

Lower probability — a recent change to pod spec resource requests or node affinity labels (not evidenced in suspectChanges, which is empty) could have altered scheduling behavior, but no suspect commit is present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to support this hypothesis.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation on the 2 eligible nodes immediately to determine current capacity vs. demand. If slots are fully occupied, identify which pods hold them and whether any are stale, leaked, or eligible for eviction.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is available and not exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a different scheduling constraint (e.g., taint, label mismatch, quota) must be investigated.

If re-running the eval probe immediately after the failure succeeds and produces all required evidence fields, the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly occupied slot) rather than sustained exhaustion.

If the 4 nodes that 'didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' are shown to have kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the affinity rules are found to be misconfigured (not intentional), the primary cause shifts to a node selector/affinity misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.

If no existing pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm resources on the 2 eligible nodes, the resource may be misconfigured or the node resource advertisement may have stopped, which would be a different failure mode than exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-create fails while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime pass in a subsequent run, the failure is not cluster-wide and may be isolated to a specific pod spec or timing window.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm resource availability across all cluster nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, so scheduling exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct infrastructure check rather than a timeout inside the agent-create probe.
Add a cluster node capacity eval that asserts at least N kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are free across the eligible node pool, alerting before the pool is fully exhausted.

Add a remote-agent pod cleanup verification eval that confirms no orphaned remote-agent pods are holding VM slots after each eval run cycle, catching cleanup failures from interrupted withCleanup paths.

Add a node affinity coverage eval that asserts the fraction of cluster nodes matching the remote-agent pod selector meets a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 50% of nodes), catching affinity misconfigurations before they cause full scheduling failures.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-25 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: 0/6 nodes are available due to 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes not matching the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the remote agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or collecting any evidence, leaving all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent and the expected-output contract entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 schedulable nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~126–152 seconds), preventing the eval runner from progressing past the createAgent call in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1918). This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is scoped to this observability eval.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 143s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

sibling.remote-agent-state: same Unschedulable / Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm message, latencyMs=151888, endedAt=2026-06-25T09:50:07.813Z

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=152216, status=fail — eval ran for ~152 seconds before the scheduler gave up, well under the outageLatencyMs=420000 threshold defined in source.infra/evals/status/features.json:185
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent — consistent with the agent pod never being created
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — no evidence was collected at any stage of the probe

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918; scheduling failure before this call returns means no agent identity or runtime response is ever captured

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:262-270: contract requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, message and asserts message containsIgnoreCase 'hello from aura' — none of these can be satisfied without a running pod
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the extended VM resource type used by peer-pod (kata containers) is fully allocated, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch reducing the schedulable pool: only 2 of 6 nodes match the remote agent pod's node affinity or node selector, and those 2 are already at kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. The remaining 4 nodes are ineligible regardless of VM resource availability.

Tertiary — cluster autoscaler not provisioning new kata-capable nodes in time: if autoscaling is configured for kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes, it may not have triggered or completed before the eval's scheduling timeout (~126–152 seconds).
Lower confidence — a recent workload spike or leaked/stuck remote agent pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them, preventing new allocations.

reproductionSteps.label: Re-run the remote-agent-runtime eval in isolation against production-api
reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow to reproduce the scheduling failure.

reproductionSteps.label: Re-run all three failing remote-agents checks together to confirm shared scheduling root cause
reproductionSteps.details: All three checks failed with the same Unschedulable reason; running them together confirms the failure is not isolated to one check.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used capacity on the 2 affinity-matching nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Use kubectl to describe the nodes that match the remote agent pod's node affinity/selector and check the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource allocatable vs. requested values.

reproductionSteps.label: List pending or running remote agent pods to identify any stuck or leaked pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots
reproductionSteps.details: Query the namespace used by remote agents for pods in Pending or Running state that hold kata.peerpods.io/vm resources but may not be actively serving traffic.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Kubernetes pod scheduling layer (kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource)
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler message in failed-check.message explicitly names Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on 2 nodes and node affinity mismatch on 4 nodes as the reasons no pod could be placed.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature — all three checks: remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature (lines 183–185) failed with the same scheduling error, indicating the entire remote agent provisioning path is blocked.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — createAgent call for remote agent type
affectedAreas.reason: The runner at line 1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote'; this call cannot complete when the underlying pod cannot be scheduled, causing the probe to time out with no evidence collected.

affectedAreas.label: Expected-output contract — remote-agent-runtime
affectedAreas.reason: The contract at lines 266–270 requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message; all are missing (expected-output.missing-required-evidence) because the pod never started.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 affinity-matching nodes in the production-api cluster to determine current utilization and whether the resource is still exhausted.
Identify and terminate any stuck or leaked remote agent pods that are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without actively serving traffic, to free capacity for new scheduling.
If autoscaling is configured for kata-capable nodes, verify the autoscaler is healthy and able to provision additional nodes; if not configured, consider manually scaling up the node pool.

Re-run all three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) after any capacity remediation to confirm the scheduling failure is resolved and evidence is collected.

Review the node affinity/selector configuration for remote agent pods to determine whether the pool of eligible nodes (currently 2 of 6) can be safely expanded to reduce the blast radius of future capacity exhaustion events.
Monitor kata.peerpods.io/vm utilization over time to establish a baseline and set alerting thresholds before the resource reaches exhaustion again.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-runtime eval to check if scheduling failure persists
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion is ongoing or was a transient spike. A pass would confirm self-resolution; a fail with the same message confirms the resource is still exhausted.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Check kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used on affinity-matching nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms whether the resource is exhausted and how many slots are in use vs. available.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Run kubectl describe node on each node matching the remote agent pod's node affinity/selector and inspect the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource capacity and current allocations.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List all remote agent pods in Pending or Running state
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether leaked pods are consuming capacity and whether the backlog has grown since the eval failure.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Query the remote agents namespace for pods in Pending state (to see backlog) and Running state (to identify any leaked or stuck pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots).

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run sibling local-agent checks to confirm failure is isolated to remote/kata path
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: If local agent checks pass while remote agent checks fail, the problem is confirmed to be specific to the kata.peerpods.io/vm scheduling path and not a broader platform issue.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect cluster autoscaler logs for kata-capable node scale-out events
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines if autoscaling is configured and functioning for kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes, or if manual intervention is needed to add capacity.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Check autoscaler logs for the time window 2026-06-25T09:45:00Z–2026-06-25T09:53:00Z to determine whether a scale-out was triggered and whether it completed or failed.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A subsequent eval run where remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, or remote-agent-runtime passes and returns non-empty evidence (orgId, agentId, etc.) would indicate the scheduling issue was transient and has self-resolved.

kubectl output showing kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity available on the affinity-matching nodes at the time of the failure would suggest the scheduler message was misleading and the root cause lies elsewhere (e.g., a quota, admission webhook, or API error).
Evidence that the 2 affinity-matching nodes were cordoned, drained, or in a NotReady state during the failure window would shift the root cause to node availability rather than resource exhaustion.

A passing run of the local-agent-create or local-agent-runtime checks (which do not use kata.peerpods.io/vm) at the same time would confirm the failure is isolated to the remote/kata peer-pod scheduling path and not a broader cluster or API outage.
Scheduler logs showing the pod was eventually scheduled but the application layer returned an error would rule out pure resource exhaustion as the cause.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm available capacity on affinity-matching nodes and fails with a warning before the resource reaches 100% utilization, providing earlier signal than a scheduling timeout.
Add a check that counts remote agent pods in Pending state for more than a configurable threshold (e.g., 60 seconds) and surfaces this as a degraded signal for the remote-agents feature.

Consider a synthetic eval that verifies at least one remote agent pod can be scheduled and reach Running state within the warning latency window (300,000 ms), distinct from the full runtime response check, to isolate scheduling failures from application-layer failures.
Add a node-pool health check eval that verifies the count of Ready, kata-capable nodes meets a minimum threshold, catching node drain or cordon events before they exhaust scheduling capacity.
